subject: art-design
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: What does 'tone' refer to in the formal elements?
options: The lightness or darkness of an area
questions.explain: Tone describes how light or dark an area is, helping to create the illusion of form.

questions.q: What is the purpose of 'annotation' in a sketchbook?
options: To explain your thinking, choices and development in words
To list the cost of materials
To fill empty space with decoration
questions.explain: Annotation uses written notes to explain your ideas, decisions and how your work is developing.

questions.q: What is the shading technique of drawing closely spaced parallel lines called?
questions.explain: Hatching builds tone using sets of parallel lines; crossing a second set over them is cross-hatching.

questions.q: The Renaissance saw a renewed interest in...
questions.explain: Renaissance artists revived classical ideals and developed realism and linear perspective.

questions.q: Two-point perspective uses how many vanishing points?
questions.explain: Two-point perspective uses two vanishing points on the horizon, typically for objects seen at a corner.

questions.q: In a landscape, objects placed at the bottom of the picture usually appear to be in the...
questions.explain: Objects lower in the picture plane normally read as nearer to the viewer, in the foreground.

questions.q: In GCSE Art, the assessment objective about 'recording' asks you to...
options: Record ideas, observations and insights relevant to your intentions
Write an essay with no images
questions.explain: The recording objective is about capturing observations and ideas, for example through drawing and photography.

options: Two sets of parallel lines crossing to build darker tone
Dotting the surface to suggest tone
questions.explain: Cross-hatching layers a second set of lines across the first to create darker, denser tone.

questions.q: In a composition, what is the 'focal point'?
options: The main area that draws the viewer's eye
The darkest area of the picture
questions.explain: The focal point is the part of the composition that attracts the viewer's attention first.

options: The appearance of texture created on a flat surface
Texture you can physically feel on the surface
questions.explain: Visual texture is the illusion of texture on a flat surface, whereas actual texture can be touched.

questions.q: Jackson Pollock is famous for which technique?
options: Dripping and pouring paint onto canvas
questions.explain: Jackson Pollock developed a 'drip' technique, pouring paint onto canvas laid on the floor.

questions.q: Which artist is closely linked to Impressionism?
questions.explain: Claude Monet was a founder of Impressionism, famous for paintings such as his water lilies.
